ref: .claude/references/targets/quasar.md (Ring protocols of a data-movement kernel); tt_metal/impl/dataflow_buffer/DataflowBuffer.md (How many txn ids)
what: Under implicit sync the runtime picks the smallest txn-id count n in [2,4] dividing num_entries/max(R,W), and the ISR credits num_entries/n per batch, so an even ring is always credited in half-ring batches whatever its depth in blocks. The target page and the perf catalog (double_buffer, trid_double_issue: depth 3-4) present ring depth as a free overlap knob; on an implicit-sync Quasar ring, raising the depth alone does not give finer in-flight blocks. Only DataflowBuffer.md shows it, in a table.
suggest: One line on the target page under Ring protocols: on implicit sync the credited batch is num_entries/n (n = smallest of 2..4 that divides), so turn the block size, not the depth, to change batch granularity; size the ring so n equals the depth you want.
